title: 正五边形内圆的半径之和
titleEn: Sum of radii in the regular pentagon

knownBest.source: Joining any interior point to the five corners cuts the pentagon into five triangles whose areas add up to ½·(sum of the point's distances to the sides)·1 = 5ρ/2, where ρ = cot(π/5)/2 is the inradius. Each distance is at least r for the centre of an inscribed circle, so 5r/2 ≤ 5ρ/2 and r ≤ ρ, attained by the incircle. The continuous problem is solved; a nine-decimal certificate cannot attain this irrational value, and no grid-optimality claim is made.
